concerns.text: Task T012 implements a 'Mock AlayaWorld' (naive_generator.py) with injected errors, directly violating FR-001 which mandates generating sequences using the 'frozen AlayaWorld model'. This semantic weakening replaces the required research target with a synthetic mock, invalidating the baseline comparison.

Tasks T012 and T021 define a 'Mock' generator and JSON token injection, violating FR-004 which requires 'dynamic prompt re-conditioning' into the AlayaWorld inference loop. The tasks fail to implement the specific architectural mechanism (prompt conditioning) required by the spec.

Task T008 instructs to 'Generate Ground Truth Subset' automatically, violating FR-007 which mandates a 'manually annotated' subset. Automated generation cannot satisfy the requirement for human-verified ground truth needed to validate CV accuracy.

Tasks T017 and T022 lack explicit orchestration to run the pipeline across 'at least 10 random seeds' as required by FR-006. Without a specific task to loop over seeds and aggregate results, the statistical t-test requirement cannot be met.

Task T014 validates CV accuracy only on the 'clean subset' (T008), violating FR-003 which requires verified detection accuracy on the 'generated video frames' (the actual drift sequences). Validation on clean data does not prove accuracy on the noisy data being measured.

Task T027 attempts to 'enforce' the 2-core CPU constraint via code checks, violating Constitution Principle VII which requires metrics to be 'measured and reported' against the constraint. Code cannot enforce hardware limits on a runner; it can only measure and fail if exceeded.
